title: INVERSIÓN AVANZADA
subtitle: Advanced inversion · énfasis y registro formal

map.center: Ponemos una expresión negativa o restrictiva al principio e invertimos: auxiliar + sujeto. Suena formal y enfático.

items: Ordena como una pregunta: have I, did she
In no time no es negativo → sin inversión

items.a: is she

items.q: Little ____ what was coming.
items.a: did we know

explain.es: La inversión consiste en colocar el auxiliar delante del sujeto —como en una pregunta— en una frase que no es pregunta. Ocurre cuando empezamos con una expresión negativa o restrictiva (never, rarely, hardly, not only, only then, under no circumstances…) y en las condicionales formales sin if (Had I known…). El significado no cambia: cambian el énfasis y el registro, que se vuelve formal, retórico o literario.
explain.en: Inversion means putting the auxiliary before the subject, as in a question, in a sentence that is not a question. It follows a fronted negative or restrictive expression and appears in formal conditionals without if. The meaning stays the same; the effect is emphasis and a formal tone.

explain.title: 1 · Adverbios negativos
explain.es: Con never (before), rarely, seldom, hardly ever, not once, at no time y nowhere al inicio, invertimos auxiliar y sujeto. Si la frase neutra no tiene auxiliar (present o past simple), añadimos do / does / did y el verbo vuelve al infinitivo. Con el verbo be invertimos el propio verbo: Rarely is he late.
explain.en: After fronted never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, not once, at no time and nowhere, invert auxiliary and subject. With no auxiliary, add do/does/did + bare infinitive.
formula: Never / Rarely / Seldom + *have / do / did / is* + sujeto + verbo

examples.en: Never have I witnessed such a remarkable recovery.
examples.es: Nunca he presenciado una recuperación tan notable.

examples.en: Rarely does the board approve a budget without amendments.
examples.es: Rara vez aprueba el consejo un presupuesto sin enmiendas.

examples.en: At no time was the public informed of the risks.
examples.es: En ningún momento se informó al público de los riesgos.

explain.title: 2 · Hardly… when / No sooner… than
explain.es: Sirven para decir que algo ocurrió justo después de otra cosa (nada más…, apenas…, en cuanto…). La primera acción va en past perfect invertido y la segunda en past simple. Ojo con la pareja: hardly / scarcely / barely … when, pero no sooner … than. Mezclarlas (no sooner… when) es un error clásico en el C1.
explain.en: One action immediately followed by another: inverted past perfect + past simple. Hardly / Scarcely / Barely … when, but No sooner … than.
formula: Hardly / Scarcely / Barely + *had* + sujeto + participio + *when* + past simple
No sooner + *had* + sujeto + participio + *than* + past simple

examples.en: Hardly had the minister begun her speech when protesters interrupted her.
examples.es: Apenas había empezado la ministra su discurso cuando unos manifestantes la interrumpieron.

examples.en: No sooner had we signed the contract than the supplier raised its prices.
examples.es: Nada más firmar el contrato, el proveedor subió los precios.

examples.en: Scarcely had the plane landed when the storm broke.
examples.es: Apenas había aterrizado el avión cuando estalló la tormenta.

explain.title: 3 · Not only… but (also)
explain.es: Sirve para sumar dos ideas con énfasis (no solo…, sino que además…). Solo se invierte la primera parte; la segunda (but … also) lleva orden normal. Also va en su posición habitual (but she also won…). Si not only no está al principio de la oración, no hay inversión: She not only won but also…
explain.en: Invert only the first clause; the but (also) clause keeps normal word order. No inversion if not only is not at the start.
formula: Not only + *aux* + sujeto + verbo…, + but + sujeto + *also* + verbo…

examples.en: Not only did the company miss its targets, but it also lost two key clients.
examples.es: La empresa no solo no alcanzó sus objetivos, sino que además perdió dos clientes clave.

examples.en: Not only is the proposal expensive, but it is also impractical.
examples.es: La propuesta no solo es cara, sino también poco práctica.

examples.en: Not only has she written three novels, but she has also directed two films.
examples.es: No solo ha escrito tres novelas, sino que también ha dirigido dos películas.

explain.title: 4 · Only… y Not until
explain.es: Con only + tiempo o condición (only then, only later, only after…, only when…, only if…, only by + -ing) y con not until, la inversión va en la oración principal, nunca en la subordinada: Only when the results arrived did we understand ✓ — Only when did the results arrive we understood. Si only acompaña al sujeto (Only Laura knew), no hay inversión.
explain.en: With only + time/condition and not until, invert the main clause, not the subordinate one. No inversion when only modifies the subject.
formula: Only when / Only after / Not until + cláusula + *aux* + sujeto + verbo
Only then / Only by + -ing + *aux* + sujeto + verbo

examples.en: Only when the audit was completed did the scale of the fraud become clear.
examples.es: Solo cuando se completó la auditoría quedó clara la magnitud del fraude.

examples.en: Not until 2019 did the law come into force.
examples.es: La ley no entró en vigor hasta 2019.

examples.en: Only by cutting costs will we survive this crisis.
examples.es: Solo recortando costes sobreviviremos a esta crisis.

explain.title: 5 · Expresiones negativas fijas
explain.es: Under no circumstances / on no account (bajo ningún concepto), in no way (en modo alguno), little (= no tenían ni idea; con know, realise, suspect, imagine) y not a single + nombre. Son típicas de normas, advertencias y relatos. Cuidado: in no time (en un abrir y cerrar de ojos) no es negativa → sin inversión.
explain.en: Under no circumstances, on no account, in no way, little and not a single… trigger inversion. In no time (= very quickly) does not.
formula: Under no circumstances / On no account + *should / must / will* + sujeto + verbo

examples.en: Under no circumstances should passwords be shared with third parties.
examples.es: Bajo ningún concepto deben compartirse las contraseñas con terceros.

examples.en: Little did they know that the deal would collapse within a week.
examples.es: Poco se imaginaban que el acuerdo se vendría abajo en una semana.

examples.en: On no account must this door be left unlocked.
examples.es: Esta puerta no debe quedarse sin cerrar con llave en ningún caso.

explain.title: 6 · So… that / Such… that
explain.es: Para enfatizar una consecuencia adelantamos so + adjetivo/adverbio o such (= tan grande, de tal calibre). Después van el verbo (be o auxiliar), el sujeto y that. Con such, el verbo es be y concuerda con el sujeto que va detrás: Such was the demand… / Such were the delays… Muy propio de prensa y literatura.
explain.en: Front so + adjective/adverb or such + be, then verb + subject + a that-clause.

examples.en: So successful was the campaign that it was extended for a further year.
examples.es: La campaña tuvo tanto éxito que se prorrogó un año más.

examples.en: Such was the demand that tickets sold out within minutes.
examples.es: Era tal la demanda que las entradas se agotaron en pocos minutos.

examples.en: So quickly did the news spread that the company issued a statement within the hour.
examples.es: La noticia se difundió tan rápido que la empresa emitió un comunicado en menos de una hora.

explain.title: 7 · Condicionales invertidas
explain.es: En registro formal podemos suprimir if e invertir: Had (3.ª condicional), Were (2.ª, también were to) y Should (1.ª, = si por casualidad). La negativa no se contrae: Had I not known ✓ — Hadn't I known. Con were, siempre were, también con I/he/she: Was I. Should you… es la fórmula estrella de los emails formales.
explain.en: In formal English, drop if and invert had, were or should. Negatives are not contracted: Had I not…

examples.en: Had we known about the strike, we would have rescheduled the meeting.
examples.es: Si hubiéramos sabido lo de la huelga, habríamos cambiado la fecha de la reunión.

examples.en: Were the government to raise taxes, consumer spending would fall.
examples.es: Si el Gobierno subiera los impuestos, el consumo caería.

examples.en: Should you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
examples.es: Si tiene cualquier duda, no dude en ponerse en contacto conmigo.

explain.title: Condicionales: de neutro a formal
head: Con if · Neutral
Sin if · Formal (inversión)
rows: If I were in your position…
If it weren't for your help…
If it hadn't been for the rain…
Had it not been for the rain…
explain.note: Solo se pueden invertir had, were y should: nunca Did I know… ni Would you need…. El not va detrás del sujeto.
explain.note_en: Only had, were and should can replace if. Not goes after the subject.

explain.title: Neutro frente a enfático
explain.es: La inversión no cambia el significado, sino el tono: más solemne, más dramático, más formal. Úsala en un essay, un informe o un discurso, no para pedir un café.
explain.en: Inversion changes the tone, not the meaning: more solemn, dramatic and formal.

cols.head: 💬 Neutro · Neutral

items.es: Ni una sola vez reconoció el presidente las inquietudes de los accionistas.

items.en: Barely had the polls closed when the first results were announced.
items.es: Apenas habían cerrado los colegios electorales cuando se anunciaron los primeros resultados.

items.en: Only if all parties agree will the treaty be ratified.
items.es: Solo si todas las partes están de acuerdo se ratificará el tratado.

items.en: Nowhere is the housing crisis more acute than in the capital.
items.es: En ningún lugar es tan grave la crisis de la vivienda como en la capital.

items.en: In no way does this statement reflect the views of the university.
items.es: Esta declaración no refleja en modo alguno la opinión de la universidad.

items.en: Had it not been for her intervention, the negotiations would have failed.
items.es: De no haber sido por su intervención, las negociaciones habrían fracasado.

items.en: Were it not for tourism, the island's economy would collapse.
items.es: Si no fuera por el turismo, la economía de la isla se hundiría.

items.en: Such was the impact of the report that the minister resigned.
items.es: Tal fue el impacto del informe que el ministro dimitió.

items.en: Only after months of negotiation was an agreement reached.
items.es: Solo tras meses de negociación se alcanzó un acuerdo.

items.en: The firm did not deny the allegations, nor did it offer an apology.
items.es: La empresa no negó las acusaciones ni ofreció disculpas.

items.en: Not a single word did he say during the entire meeting.
items.es: No dijo ni una sola palabra en toda la reunión.

explain.note: Todas estas expresiones solo provocan inversión cuando van al principio de la oración. En posición normal, orden normal: I have never seen it / We rarely go out.
explain.note_en: These expressions only trigger inversion when they come first in the clause.

items.bad: Never I have seen such a mess.
items.good: Never have I seen such a mess.
items.why: Negativa al inicio → auxiliar delante del sujeto.

items.bad: Rarely we go out on weekdays.
items.good: Rarely do we go out on weekdays.
items.why: Sin auxiliar, hay que añadir do / does / did.
items.why_en: No auxiliary? Add do / does / did.

items.bad: Little they knew what was coming.
items.good: Little did they know what was coming.
items.why: Con did, el verbo va en infinitivo: know, no <s>knew</s>.

items.bad: No sooner had we arrived when the alarm went off.
items.good: No sooner had we arrived than the alarm went off.
items.why: No sooner … than; hardly / scarcely … when.

items.bad: Not only she speaks Chinese, but she also speaks Arabic.
items.good: Not only does she speak Chinese, but she also speaks Arabic.
items.why: Not only al inicio → inversión en la 1.ª parte.

items.bad: Only when did I read the report I understood it.
items.good: Only when I read the report did I understand it.
items.why: Se invierte la oración principal, no la de when.

items.bad: Hadn't I been so busy, I would have helped.
items.good: Had I not been so busy, I would have helped.
items.why: En la condicional invertida no se contrae el not.

items.bad: Was I in your position, I would resign.
items.good: Were I in your position, I would resign.
items.why: Condicional invertida: siempre were, también con I.

items.es: Escribe la frase neutra: I had never seen such chaos.
Lleva la expresión negativa o restrictiva al principio: Never…
items.en: Move the negative expression to the front.

items.es: Busca el primer auxiliar (have, be, will, can, should…). Si no hay, usa do / does / did en el tiempo correcto y deja el verbo en infinitivo.
items.en: Find the first auxiliary; if there isn't one, add do / does / did.

items.es: Pon el auxiliar delante del sujeto, como en una pregunta: Never had I seen such chaos.
items.en: Put the auxiliary before the subject.

items.es: Con only when / only after / not until, invierte la principal; con not only, solo la primera parte.
items.en: Only when / not until: invert the main clause. Not only: the first clause only.

items.es: Revisa el registro: ¿texto formal, discurso, relato? En una charla informal, mejor la versión neutra.
items.en: Check the register: formal text, speech or narrative?

lines.en: Did the company know about the safety problems before the launch?
lines.es: ¿Sabía la empresa de los problemas de seguridad antes del lanzamiento?

lines.en: Absolutely not. At no time were we informed of any defect.
lines.es: En absoluto. En ningún momento se nos informó de ningún defecto.

lines.en: So when did you find out?
Only when the first complaints came in did we realise how serious it was.
lines.es: Solo cuando llegaron las primeras quejas nos dimos cuenta de la gravedad.

lines.en: And what have you done since then?
Not only have we recalled every unit, but we have also offered full refunds.
lines.es: No solo hemos retirado todas las unidades, sino que también hemos ofrecido reembolsos completos.

lines.en: Can you guarantee it won't happen again?
lines.es: ¿Puede garantizar que no volverá a ocurrir?

lines.en: Under no circumstances will we allow this to happen again. Should any customer have concerns, our helpline is open 24/7.
lines.es: Bajo ningún concepto permitiremos que vuelva a ocurrir. Si algún cliente tiene dudas, nuestra línea de atención está abierta 24 horas.

explain.title: Truco del registro
explain.es: Piensa en la inversión como en un traje de gala 🎩: perfecta en un essay, un informe, un discurso o un email formal (Should you…), pero rara en una charla con amigos, donde solo sobreviven fórmulas como Little did I know… En el writing del C1, una o dos inversiones bien colocadas demuestran range; diez seguidas suenan artificiales.
explain.en: Inversion is formal dress: perfect for essays, reports, speeches and formal emails, odd in casual chat. In a C1 writing task, use one or two, not ten.

exercises.title: ¿Inversión o no?
exercises.es: Imagina que cada expresión va al principio de la frase. ¿Obliga a invertir (aux + sujeto) o no? Escríbela en su caja.
exercises.en: Imagine each expression starts the sentence. Does it trigger inversion?

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el artículo. Marca T o F y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Five years ago, Brightwave Energy was on the verge of collapse. Rarely had a company fallen so far so fast: its shares had lost 80% of their value, and not once in three years had it reported a profit. Little did investors suspect that the firm was about to stage one of the most remarkable recoveries in the sector's history.

No sooner had Elena Ruiz been appointed chief executive than she began to dismantle the old management structure. Not only did she sell off unprofitable divisions, but she also invested heavily in solar storage, a technology that most analysts considered too risky. "Under no circumstances will we return to the old way of doing things," she told shareholders at her first annual meeting.

Only when the first contracts with European utilities were signed did the markets begin to take notice. Today, Brightwave employs over 4,000 people. Had Ruiz listened to her critics, says one board member, the company would almost certainly have disappeared. Such has been its success that rivals are now copying its strategy.

items.q: Before Ruiz arrived, Brightwave had been profitable for three years.
items.why: Not once in three years had it reported a profit.

items.q: Investors expected the company to recover.
Ruiz started changing the management structure immediately after her appointment.
items.why: No sooner had she been appointed than…

items.q: Most analysts supported her investment in solar storage.
items.why: Most analysts considered it too risky.

items.q: When did the markets begin to take notice?
items.a: When the first contracts with European utilities were signed.

items.q: Rewrite with if: "Had Ruiz listened to her critics, the company would almost certainly have disappeared."
items.a: If Ruiz had listened to her critics, the company would almost certainly have disappeared.

items.q: Copy the sentence with Not only.
items.a: Not only did she sell off unprofitable divisions, but she also invested heavily in solar storage.

items.q: Rewrite without inversion: "Such has been its success that rivals are now copying its strategy."
items.a: Its success has been so great that rivals are now copying its strategy.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe frases propias en registro formal. Usa una inversión distinta en cada una.
exercises.en: Write your own formal sentences. Use a different inversion in each.

items.q: Termina un email formal con una condicional invertida (Should you…).
items.a: Ej.: Should you require any further details, please do not hesitate to contact me.

items.q: Escribe la primera frase de un discurso de agradecimiento con Never…
items.a: Ej.: Never have I felt so honoured to stand before such a distinguished audience.

items.q: Describe un error del pasado con Had I… o Had I not…
items.a: Ej.: Had I read the contract more carefully, I would not have lost my deposit.

items.q: Escribe una norma de seguridad con Under no circumstances u On no account.
items.a: Ej.: On no account should visitors enter the laboratory without safety glasses.

items.q: Cuenta una sorpresa con Little did I know… y sigue con No sooner… than.
items.a: Ej.: Little did I know that my new boss was an old classmate. No sooner had I walked in than she recognised me.

checklist.es: Invierto auxiliar + sujeto tras never, rarely, seldom, little, at no time…
checklist.en: I can invert after negative adverbials.

checklist.es: Añado do / does / did cuando la frase no tiene auxiliar.
checklist.en: I add do / does / did when there is no auxiliary.
I know hardly … when and no sooner … than.

checklist.es: Con only when / not until invierto la oración principal.
checklist.en: With only when / not until I invert the main clause.

checklist.es: Escribo condicionales formales: Had I known, Were I, Should you.
Sé que in no time, hardly anyone y only + sujeto no invierten.
checklist.en: I know when there is no inversion.

checklist.es: Uso la inversión en textos formales sin abusar de ella.
checklist.en: I use inversion in formal texts, without overdoing it.
